# Disagreement Log — MMT Section 6 (4QMMT Section C: Exhortation)

## Summary
- **Total disagreements:** 13
- **Section:** C (Exhortation to the recipient)
- **Nature:** Key theological phrases, historical rendering, rhetorical register

---

### Disagreement 1 — Line 6:1: "evil" vs. "wrongdoing"
- **EMET:** "evil" (literal of ra')
- **LOGOS:** "evil" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "wrongdoing" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "evil" — ra' is "evil" in biblical Hebrew. "Wrongdoing" narrows the semantic range.

### Disagreement 2 — Line 6:3: "saw" vs. "perceived" vs. "can see"
- **EMET:** "we saw" (literal of ra'inu)
- **LOGOS:** "we perceived" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "we can see" (dynamic, present tense)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "we saw" — past tense, simple verb, faithful to the Hebrew. See also Section 2 ruling.

### Disagreement 3 — Line 6:5: "works of the Torah" vs. "practices required by the Torah"
- **EMET:** "works of-the-Torah" (literal of ma'ase ha-torah)
- **LOGOS:** "works of the Torah" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "practices required by the Torah" (dynamic expansion)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "works of the Torah" — the document's title phrase. Must be preserved in its compact form for theological and scholarly reasons. See also Section 2 ruling.

### Disagreement 4 — Line 6:6: "straighten" vs. "direct aright" vs. "set straight"
- **EMET:** "that-He-straighten your counsel" (literal of yashar)
- **LOGOS:** "to direct your counsel aright" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "to set your thinking straight" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "to direct your counsel aright" — see Section 2 ruling. PNEUMA's "set your thinking straight" is colloquial.

### Disagreement 5 — Line 6:6: "counsel of Belial" vs. "schemes of Belial"
- **EMET:** "counsel of-Belial" (literal of 'atsat Beliya'al)
- **LOGOS:** "counsel of Belial" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "schemes of Belial" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "counsel of Belial" — 'atsah means "counsel/advice," not "schemes." The term implies deliberate, calculated evil counsel, not mere plotting.

### Disagreement 6 — Line 6:7: "end of time" vs. "in the end"
- **EMET:** "at-the-end of-time" (literal of qets ha-'et)
- **LOGOS:** "at the end of time" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "in the end" (dynamic, simplified)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "at the end of time" — the eschatological phrase qets ha-'et must be preserved. PNEUMA's "in the end" strips it of apocalyptic significance.

### Disagreement 7 — Line 6:8: "reckoned to you as righteousness" vs. "credited to you as a righteous act"
- **EMET:** "it-will-be-reckoned to-you as-righteousness" (literal, echoing Gen 15:6)
- **LOGOS:** "it shall be reckoned to you as righteousness" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "it will be credited to you as a righteous act" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "it shall be reckoned to you as righteousness" — the most theologically significant phrase in MMT. "Reckoned" preserves the Gen 15:6 echo (va-yachsheveha lo tsedaqah). PNEUMA's "credited as a righteous act" subtly shifts the theology from imputed status to evaluated deed.

### Disagreement 8 — Line 6:10–11: "in the days of" vs. "during the reign of"
- **EMET:** "in-the-days-of Solomon" (literal of bi-yemei)
- **LOGOS:** "in the days of Solomon" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "during the reign of Solomon" (dynamic, specifies royal context)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "in the days of Solomon" — the standard biblical temporal formula. PNEUMA's "during the reign of" is accurate but loses the idiomatic biblical phrasing.

### Disagreement 9 — Line 6:14: "have come" vs. "have already come to pass" vs. "have already taken place"
- **EMET:** "have-come" (literal of ba'u)
- **LOGOS:** "have already come to pass" (formal, adds "already")
- **PNEUMA:** "have already taken place" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "have already come to pass" — "already" is justified by the author's retrospective argument, and "come to pass" is the standard biblical idiom.

### Disagreement 10 — Line 6:17: "feared" vs. "revered" vs. "honored"
- **EMET:** "feared [the Torah]" (literal of yare')
- **LOGOS:** "revered [the Torah]" (formal, elevated)
- **PNEUMA:** "honored [the Torah]" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "feared [the Torah]" — yare' fundamentally means "to fear." In the context of Torah observance, the fear-dimension (awe, trembling obedience) is theologically operative. "Revered" and "honored" soften this.

### Disagreement 11 — Line 6:18: "seekers of the Torah" vs. "ones who sought to follow the Torah"
- **EMET:** "seekers of-the-Torah" (literal of dorshei ha-torah)
- **LOGOS:** "seekers of the Torah" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "ones who sought to follow the Torah" (dynamic expansion)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "seekers of the Torah" — dorshei ha-torah is a technical sectarian self-designation. PNEUMA's expansion dissolves the technical term into a generic description.

### Disagreement 12 — Line 6:19: "man of pious deeds" vs. "man known for his faithful deeds"
- **EMET:** "man of-pious-deeds" (literal of ish chasadim)
- **LOGOS:** "man of pious deeds" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "man known for his faithful deeds" (dynamic, adds "known for")
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "man of pious deeds" — the compact Hebrew designation. PNEUMA's expansion adds interpretive content ("known for") not in the source.

### Disagreement 13 — Line 6:22: "uprightness" vs. "integrity"
- **EMET:** "in-uprightness" (literal of be-yosher)
- **LOGOS:** "in uprightness" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "with integrity" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "in uprightness" — yosher means "straightness, uprightness." "Integrity" is close but shifts toward a modern ethical concept. "Uprightness" preserves the Hebrew root's concrete imagery of straightness.
